title: Knowledge-graph learning prioritizes experimentally examined Alzheimer genes
summary: A learned knowledge-graph model nominated candidate Alzheimer-associated genes for neuronal, autopsy and cell-assay follow-up. The study highlights candidate associations rather than establishing causes of human disease. Small samples, noisy negative labels and an internal discrepancy in reported knockdown-hit counts constrain interpretation; those counts are not treated as reconciled.
organization: University of New Mexico; University of Gothenburg; University of Copenhagen

evidence.tested: Selected predicted genes received biological screening.
evidence.unknown: Independent validation, human causality and therapeutic benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: MPxgb(AD) knowledge-graph XGBoost supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary publisher PDF abstract and model description, publisher date and PubMed affiliations; detailed prior Methods review retained, direct PMC retrieval blocked.
